## Ready next (first 15 MVP todo leaves whose milestone deps are done)

- `6.1.6` Undo a failed `put` without rehashing the term arenas: `Arena::truncate` rebuilds the whole table under the write lock, O(terms) per rejected document (found in the 6.1 review) (M6)
- `6.1.7` Cache `MemtableView::df` if term statistics become hot: it walks the posting chain under the read lock on every call. The count is the view's `(docs, version)` cutoff, so it cannot reuse a live counter on the term, and a cache has to be keyed by that cutoff and bounded (found in 7.2) (M6)
- `6.3.11` Flush without re-indexing: build the segment from the memtable's postings instead of analyzing every document again (ADR-0029, found in 6.3.1); bench the flush before and after (M6)
- `6.4.5` Prune the commit's tombstone lookups by each segment's footer id range (`Segment::id_range`), once open or `Segment::verify` checks `min_id`/`max_id` against the `IdMap` (a wrong range would leave an older copy live). Helps time-ordered ids only; random ids (UUIDs) span every range. Bench `commit_inserts_*` before and after (found in 6.4.3: 64 segments double a 2 000-document commit) (M6)
- `6.4.7` Per-segment id membership filter (e.g. a Bloom filter section) so a commit skips segments that cannot hold an id, for random ids that id ranges do not prune; a format change (SPEC §5.3, ADR, golden file) (found in the 6.4 review) (M6)
- `6.5.6` Streaming merge writer: encode the merged sections while the inputs are read, so a merge holds no more than a block per section instead of the whole merged segment in a `SegmentBuilder` (ADR-0031 item 8, found in 6.5.2) (M6)
- `6.5.7` Merge throughput: a merge-only postings reader that decodes whole lists (no per-term `Postings` cursor), and regrouping without a sort; goal: `segment_merge/copy_8` faster than `segment/add` on the same run (internal bench, `docs/benchmarks.md`; not a claim, BENCHMARKS.md) (M6)
- `6.5.8` Engine-driven container compaction (SPEC §4.6): `Database` names the live frames (the manifest's, plus the obsolete frames still referenced, 6.5.4) and the WAL range, compacts when dead space reaches the ratio, and publishes the relocated manifest (`Manifest::relocate`) (found in 6.5.4) (M6)
- `6.5.9` Merges that survive concurrent deletes: re-apply the deletions committed to its inputs since the plan to the merged segment (a docid map kept with the result) instead of discarding it (ADR-0032 item 4, found in 6.5.3) (M6)
- `6.6.6` Refresh a `ReadOnlyDatabase` in place: a new snapshot from the next manifest and the WAL frames written since, instead of a reopen (ADR-0033 Alternatives, found in 6.6.2) (M6)
- `6.6.8` `persia verify` with custom analyzers, once a schema can name an analyzer registered with `AnalyzerRegistry::register` (today `AnalyzerRef` accepts built-ins only, SPEC §6.2.2): a way to load them in the CLI, or a replay that validates records without analyzing their `text` fields (found in 6.6.7) (M6)
- `6.6.10` `persia inspect container` (CLI, read-only): the superblock (`seq`, `wal_start`, `log_end`), every frame from `wal_start` (kind, offset, length, `frame_seq`, whether after `log_end`), Manifest frames after `log_end` with their `seq`, and with `--id` the WAL records naming a document id. Replaces the throwaway debug test the 6.6.9 triage needed (crash-triage skill) (M6)
- `7.3.5` (v1.0) Term proximity scoring: a bonus from the minimum span, or the pair distance, of the query terms, using positions already indexed (5.3.4). The bonus must keep pruning bounds valid (MaxScore and block-max WAND, SPEC §7.2, §7.3) (M7)
- `7.4.7` A disjunction for many clauses (relaxation expansions, SPEC §7.6: up to 50 prefix or fuzzy terms): a heap instead of a scan of every clause per document, and phrase candidates that copy positions only while starts survive; bench `search_top10/or` with 50 clauses before and after (found in the 7.4 review) (M7)
- `7.4.8` Prune conjunctions and `should` clauses beside `must` with block bounds (block-max AND, required plus optional as Lucene's ReqOpt): today a threshold reaches only a term, a pure `should` disjunction and what `must_not`/`boost` wrap (SPEC §7.3, found in 7.4.4) (M7)
- … and 35 more
